text: This is a poor welcome, my lord.
We have come to ask but a pittance.
You obstruct the crusade, my lord, with your parsimony.
But your majesty already has my whole fortune willingly given but six months since.
There is no more. My coffers are empty.
Your words are more generous than your purse, Lord Ranulph.
If you speak truth, if we have your whole fortune.
My father is of ill health, Sir Gilles.
Take my lands, my goods, my chattels, even the robes I stand in.
But spare me my surviving son.
We shall see, my lord, if your fealty is as slender as your fortune.
Your son shall meet our champion on the morrow.
We shall retire and dream sweet dreams.
Calm yourselves. There's no cause for alarm.
You didn't set the coordinates for here by any chance.
Could this be a Black Guardian trap?
I have no need of aid from Lucifer.
We tell you there's naught to fear.
Do our demons come to visit us?
Makes a nice change for you not to take everything in your stride, I must say.
He even seems pleased to see us.
The one who lost something in the wash.
Well, could put it like that.
His meticulous shirt turned out to be the crown jewels.
We're still three months away from Magna Carta.
Her name is Tegan, Your Majesty.
Come rejoice with us in a trial by combat.
Let them be seated by us.
Your Majesty, if I may make so bold.
If this is trial by combat, Your Majesty, there is clearly a victor and a vanquished.
We take your counsel, oh demon.
Heed him not, whoever you are.
You are welcome at Fitzwilliam Castle.
Soon we shall sit at meat.
Betimes you may wish to withdraw.
Conduct my guests to their chamber.
Look at the size of that bed.
What are we doing here, anyway?
We were invited for a meal.
How long are you planning to stay?
Do you know it's just sunk in?
The king takes the oath today.
To take the cross as a crusader.
Perhaps they got that bit wrong.
Well, all I care about is getting back to the TARDIS where it's nice and warm.
No wonder they forced him to sign Magna Carta.
Bet there was something in it about under-heated housing.
Forced him to sign Magna Carta.
He was as much for it as anyone.
I would know who or what you are.
He is as proud as you.
But at the present, my concern is for the king.
And who are these beings he calls demons?
I must ask the lady Isabella to accompany me.
Your lady is to be held in custody.
To be held in custody against your continued good behavior toward our sovereign lord, the king.
The king is a guest in my house.
He would not use me thus.
He would and does, my lord.
He sends to Atenoi to preserve peaches.
A new cider will be provided when he dies.
The king shall lack no comfort while within these walls.
I'll tell you anything you want to know.
But you speak nothing but madness.
I've told you who I am and where I come from.
I am the king's man, like my father.
And what is this doctor's purpose?
Well, perhaps I can loosen your tongue.
There really is no need for any of this.
If you do not, I most assuredly will kill you!
Why is youth given to such extravagance?
It appears, my lady, you will not be without companionship.
But at least, I will be able to examine this demon's engine.
engine. Are you saying King John was a good man? Well, given the times he lives in, yes.
But don't take my word for it. You'll be able to judge for yourself. Nobody forced Magna Carta
from him. He could have crushed that rebellion as easily as that. What have you demons made
of the king? He is bewitched. First he takes my whole fortune, and now he has made my lady
a hostage. How can he question my loyalty? There is none more loyal than I. We are not
demons, and we've done no harm to the king, or to anyone, nor do we intend any...
Whence come you? From an outer province. And this strange attire? Yes. Please believe that
we are friends. If you're in trouble, I would like to help if I can. Leave us, and fetch
warm vestments. You wear three? Yes, yes, sir. We seem to have mislaid, Turlough.
How long has the king been here? Since yesterday. But he is not himself. He is not as I know
him. Where could he be ill? In rude health. He rode from London yesterday, and then to
a stag hunt to bring down the only kill. This is Gilles. I like not this man. I can't say
I care for him much myself. A French knight. Is he the only Frenchman with the king? I
know not. He has never favoured Frenchmen before this. Even renegades from the king
of France. Could Sir Gilles be bringing some precious?
Some influence on the king? The king is influenced by none. The king I know is resolute and firm
of purpose. When does he return to London? I know not. And no word from the city. My
cousin was summoned there by the king a week since, and he's not returned. Why? And why
no word concerning him? Your cousin was summoned to London? Aye. To take the Crusader's oath.
Lord Doctor? What if your guest was not the king? Not the king? Then who? An imposter.
I have known and served my sovereign lord for many years. No imposter could be so like.
Oh, be vigilant, my lord. I suspect things are not what they seem. You are a sorcerer.
No, no. And I ask you to trust me, please. You can trust us. You will join my household
at meet. Thank you. We would be delighted.
When it pleases you. Warmer? Yes. Shouldn't we find out what's happened to Turlough? We
will. I don't feel safe here. A while longer, then we'll go.
Name yourself, sir knight. Geoffrey de Lacy, cousin to Ranulf Fitzwilliam. And your name?
Gilles Lestrame, king's champion. Why, then, are you not with the king? I am. How can
that be, since the king is in London? No. The king is here. Born on eagle's wings. I
left the king in the tower this morning. You lie. Take him. Our demons welcome. Come join.
Turlough. Stop fussing. Can you not help us?
I wish I could. Can you not call on hell? I could. But then so could you. With a better
chance of success, I fancy. I do hope they've found a better use for it. A better use?
If he's not the king, who is he? Why? Do you seriously expect me to answer that? Why
didn't he react like everybody else? Why wasn't he scared? And why are we his demons? Could
he be the devil? I only said could.
Lutes. Let us have the lutes.
We sing in praise of total war. Against the Saracen we are poor. To free the tomb of
Christ our Lord. We'll put the known world to the sword. There is no glory greater than
to serve with gold the sword of God.
O son of man, no riches here on earth shall see. No scutage in eternity.
And now, sire, for some additional entertainment.
And who is to delight in her embrace?
Sire, this is my cousin Geoffrey de Lacy, a loyal knight. You summoned him to London
but a week since to take the Crusader's oath.
And he has seen fit to disobey that summons.
I left your Majesty in London four hours since.
The King has been here since yesterday.
Let the maiden reward such mendacity.
Your cousin is guilty of lese-majeste, my lord.
You must be on your guard.
But, our demon, you too would beg for mercy.
Oh, indeed, no, sire, but surely such a fate as two miles
would not boiling in oil be a more fitting end?
It must be a decade, our champion, since we boiled in oil.
We accept your counsel, O demon.
I thank your majesty, but I was not suggesting alternative retribution.
My interruption was provoked by shock.
Yes, I was quite shocked at Tazil's monstrous lack of good taste.
Who dares to question my good taste?
In my view, it is the worst possible taste to even think about
following the king's own quite remarkable performance.
I am insulted. He is said to be the best swordsman in France.
Fortunately, we are in England. May I?
Thank you. I hope I don't disgrace it.
In case of accidents... Doctor, don't do it.
Has our demon mortal life to lose?
Oh, my dear doctor, you have been naive.
